MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  JUNE 20, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-
20 and fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19)
pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Hill called the meeting to order at 6:3 I p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Kraig Hill, Vice Chair Dennis Robert Smith. and Commissioners Jeffrey
  Jennings, John Mazza, and Mark Wetton

  ALSO PRESENT: Richard Mollica, Planning Director; Trevor Rusin, Assistant City
  Attorney; Jessica Thompson, Senior Planner; Philip Coronel, Assistant Planner; Lauren
  Doyel, Coastal Engineer and Geotechnical Reviewer; and Rebecca Evans, Recording
  Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda as recommended by staff and to continue Item No. 5.A. to July
  18, 2022.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on June 10, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Ryan Ernbree stated the City approved a project for the Santa Monica Community
  College-Malibu Campus, yet a noncompliant tower was installed. He asked why
  the tower had not been referred to code enforcement contract prosecutors. ordered
  to be torn down and laid flat on the ground during pending application processes.

  Jo Drummond expressed agreement with Ryan Embree that the wireless tower was
  unattractive, unnecessarily large and should be removed. She requested an
  explanation of what staff was doing to resolve this.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION I STAFF COMMENTS

  Commissioner Mazza and Chair Hill asked the Commission to dedicate the meeting
  in honor of the late Malibu Architect Harry Gesner.

  Commissioner Jennings asked for clarification from Planning Director Mol lica on
  his statement that Option 4 projects had been placed on hold, requested the Planning
  Department’s definition of on hold, and asked if planners had ceased to work on
  projects designated as on hold. He also asked if projects which previously received
  planning approval were permitted to continue forward through Building and Safety
  up to the point of not issuing building permits. He asked who made the decision to
  temporarily suspend Option 4.

  In response to Commissioner Jennings, Planning Director Mollica clarified that on
  hold meant that for anyone with an application currently under review, Planning
  was not currently issuing approvals or notices of application to start the 21-day
  process. Staff continued to review pending applications but would not yet issue
  decisions. Projects already under construction had been allowed to move forward
  due to approval prior to receipt of the letter from the California Coastal
  Commission. The matter was likely to go before the City Council for direction, The
  decision to place a hold on Option 4 was made by the City Attorney’s Office, the
  City Manager and the Planning Director.

  Commissioner Jennings stated that it appeared the applications in the Planning
  Department were being treated differently than applications now in Building and
  Safety, which had been moving forward with no hold and were eligible to receive
  stamps of approval. Planning Director Mollica confirmed that was true, because a
  decision was rendered prior to receipt of the email from the California Coastal
  Commission. Determinations were based on the date of the issuance of the
  Director’s decision.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of June 20, 2022
  Page 3 of 10

Commissioner Jennings asked whether the 45 already approved Administrative
Plan Review-Woolsey Fire projects reported included the 26 placed on hold, or
were in addition to the 26. Senior Planner Thompson confirmed that the 26 placed
on hold were included in the 45 proposed projects reported. Planning Director
Mollica noted that anyone who applied to use the exemption in Option 4 had been
put on hold pending further conversation with the California Coastal Commission.

Commissioner Jennings asked if the City had determined how to move these
projects forward, perhaps as California Coastal Commission administrative
applications, should the California Coastal Commission deny the use of Option 4
and for an explanation of why variances were not progressing in the interim.
Planning Director Mollica stated that Planning had not yet determined the process
to move these projects forward pending a meeting with California Coastal
Commission management and noted that there were costs associated with variance
approvals.

Assistant City Attorney Rusin suggested that Commissioner Jennings follow up
individually with the Planning Director because the discussion topic was not on the
current agenda. Commissioner Jennings stated he had sent a letter the prior week
and received no reply. Planning Director Mollica confirmed he had been on
vacation the prior week but stated he would follow up with Commissioner Jennings.

Chair Hill asked what associated costs would be incurred if the applications should
have to be processed as Coastal Development Permits with Director level approval.
Planning Director Mollica explained that the costs would be related to the specific
scope of work for each project. If the property were held by the original owner at
time of the Woolsey Fire, Planning would have to look at whether costs were
eligible for fee waiver or return to Council on that issue as well.

Commissioner Mazza asked if Planning had an answer on whether Howdy’s
Sonrisa Café’s outdoor extension was considered enclosed or unenclosed space.
Senior Planner Thompson stated that she conducted the analysis and would report
on that issue during the hearing for the related item.

Commissioner Wetton noted that his questions were similar to the Option 4 issues
al ready eloquently expressed by Commissioner Jennings.

Vice Chair Smith expressed concern that Commissioner Jennings’ letter to
Planning had not yet received a response despite his long-term service to the City
of Malibu and his status as a Woolsey-Fire victim.

Chair Hill asked if the Klein project had been heard by the California Coastal
Commission and the result if the matter had been decided.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of June 20. 2022
  Page4of 10

  In response to Chair Hill, Commissioner Mazza stated the Kleins agreed to move
  the house back, away from the creek, raise it up and to tear it down in the future if
  it became subject to wave uprush.

  Chair Hill recalled the definition of enclosed space as sixty percent, related to the
  Floor Area Ratio. He asked for clarification on the sections of the code regarding
  enclosed space. the location of the formal definition and whether there was any
  interpretation of the word bulk other than volume.

  Planning Director Mollica stated that commercial development standards use Floor
  Area Ratio and the term enclosed was in the definition section. While there was no
  formal definition, in general bulk referred to size and massing as descriptive terms.

  Senior Planner Thompson noted the definition was in an unusual spot under
  definitions titled “Buildings, Enclosed.”

  Chair Hill asked when the Local Implementation Plan 13.4.6. exemption for
  structures destroyed by natural disaster was put in place, after the 1 993 fire or
  following the Woolsey Fire.

  In response to Chair Hill, Planning Director Mollica explained the exemption had
  no relation to the City, the exemption came from the California Coastal Act and
  was independent of the Malibu replacement policies and history. Malibu City codes
  at the time were stricter and did not include the ten percent addition. Malibu
  changed the fire rebuild ordinance and the Malibu Municipal Code to align with
  the rebuild process in the California Coastal Act.

  Commissioner Jennings confirmed the City of Malibu exemption language was
  imposed by the Coastal Act, which was imposed by the California State Legislature.
  It was purely statutory language out of the California Coastal Act.

  Planning Director Mollica informed the Commission the Malibu Middle and High
  School campus Environmental Impact Report was scheduled for City Council on
  July II, 2022 and the applicant had submitted an updated Specific Plan with the
  Cloverfield lot removed.

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Chair 1-lill seconded a motion to deny Planning
  Commission Resolution No. 22-43 based on the inability to make findings 2, 3 and

  Commercial Visitor Serving-One zoning district and the Civic Center Northeast

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT

  Based on the applicant’s request for continuance. Commissioner Mazza withdrew

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion to
